extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in US postwar policy and domestic economic measures
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper article summarizing contemporary US domestic economic debates (price controls, tax policy, banking measures), foreign aid (Marshall Plan/interim aid), food-conservation drives, and international treaty ratification. Covers proposals, committee hearings, and official statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOP economic program — tax slashing and spending economy
rubrics_metrics.description: A new call for tax slashing, accompanied by economy in Government spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a multi-point Republican alternative to the Administration's controls; presented as item 1 of a GOP program under discussion by party leaders (Chairman Wolcott (R., Mich.) and others).

rubrics_metrics.name: GOP economic program — voluntary industry-wide price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary industry-wide action looking toward price adjustments. Agreements made for this purpose might be exempted from anti-trust laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A voluntary approach is intended to rule out compulsory price-wage and rationing controls requested by the President; details of how exemptions from anti-trust laws would be arranged were under discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOP economic program — extension of export controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension of export controls, to provide a measure of protection of the domestic economy against heavy foreign shipments (and inflation that might be caused by this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as item 3 of the GOP plan; intended to preserve domestic supplies/prices while allowing continued foreign sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOP economic program — authority over railway freight cars
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to control the use of railway freight cars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among GOP program elements (to manage logistics/transport related to economic stabilization); details not specified in the excerpt.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOP economic program — foreign currency stabilization
rubrics_metrics.description: A program for stabilization of foreign currencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 5 of the GOP plan; details of the program were not disclosed in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOP economic program — encourage government bond sales
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as item 6 of the GOP plan; framed as part of fiscal measures to stabilize the economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOP economic program — continuation of rent controls
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 7 in the GOP program list; proposed as part of controlling cost-of-living pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary approach versus compulsory price-wage/rationing controls
rubrics_metrics.description: The voluntary approach would rule out the President’s request for authority to use compulsory price-wage and rationing controls on a limited basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Republicans signaled preference for voluntary measures (industry agreements, voluntary conservation) rather than restoring compulsory controls; this distinction affects whether the administration can impose mandatory controls during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of emergency/aid program by independent agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for administration of the emergency program, as well as any subsequent long-range program, by an independent [agency].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed safeguard/pending amendment to establish an independent administrative body to run emergency foreign-aid programs, rather than centralizing control in a pre-existing agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit government purchases to declared surplus commodities
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict all Government buying under the bill to commodities declared surplus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pending amendment intended to limit the scope of government commodity purchases to avoid pushing domestic prices higher; part of a set of proposed restrictions on the interim aid bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose price ceilings on government purchases as a safeguard
rubrics_metrics.description: Impose price ceilings on Government purchases as a safe-guard against raising domestic prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendment language aimed at preventing emergency foreign purchases from bidding up US prices; specifics of ceilings not provided in excerpt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce total interim aid authorization (amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments proposed to reduce the total authorization for interim aid — suggestions ranged down to as low as $400,000,000 from higher figures ($590M–$597M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of several parliamentary tactics to limit or reshape the aid measure before final passage; reflects fiscal constraint as evaluative criterion for the bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aid-contract safeguards — cut-off if Communists seize control
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency help can be cut off if Communists seize control of recipient governments; additional 'safeguards' will be written into contracts made with those governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance given by Under Secretary of State Robert A. Lovett to Senators; key procedural condition intended to limit long-term commitments and respond to changed political circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary food-conservation program components
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanded voluntary program including meatless Tuesdays and eggless Thursdays; invitation to distillers to plan continued grain conservation after a shutdown; requests to brewers to curtail use of wheat and corn; public urged to eat at least one less slice of bread a day; baking industry asked to curtail 'consignment selling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announced by the cabinet food group (Anderson, Harriman, Lovett) as measures to save grain for European relief and check domestic inflation; emphasis on voluntary community and industry cooperation rather than compulsory measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senator Flanders' voluntary rationing proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A voluntary rationing program to fix the maximum number of pounds of meat each person should eat a week; those who ate more would be 'branded' as a 'social menace.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flanders advocated this as stronger voluntary measure (distinct from ad-hoc 'meatless Tuesday'); he preferred voluntary methods first but proposed punitive social labeling for wilful noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving quotas for hotels and restaurants
rubrics_metrics.description: Serving quotas should be fixed for hotels and restaurants, and any that did not go along ought to be labeled as trying to wreck our economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested as part of community-level measures to enforce conservation goals; presented rhetorically by a speaker urging stricter adherence to voluntary programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Reserve special reserve proposal to curb credit expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the nation’s banks to set up a special reserve of untouched money as a brake on credit expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marriner Eccles (Federal Reserve Board chairman) urged the Senate Banking Committee to consider this plan as a measure to curb inflationary credit growth; faced opposition from bankers who considered it inimical to their interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEA findings on commodity-futures trading practices and tax consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: CEA investigation disclosed trading practices which could be used for postponing, reducing, or completely avoiding payment of income taxes — example: treating futures profits as long-term capital gains (taxed at a lower effective rate) and manipulating transaction dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article details an example where a trader buys future-delivery cotton, sells months later but leaves dates open so profit appears as long-term capital gain; implies need to consider fixing margin requirements and closing tax loopholes related to commodity futures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-American defense treaty ratification requirement and collective-defense obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Inter-American defense treaty pledges nineteen nations to act jointly against any aggression in the hemisphere; to become effective it must be ratified by the listed nations (Dominican Republic, Guatemala, Costa Rica, etc., including the United States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for treaty effectiveness; contains the substantive standard that an attack on any signatory is treated as an attack on all (collective defense).
